title: How to Become an Expert in English (or Anything Else!)
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: Someone very skilled or knowledgeable in a particular area.
The ability to identify patterns or information quickly from memory.
Information about how well you did, used to improve.
Repeatedly doing an activity to get better at it.
The setting or conditions where learning or practicing happens.
Something difficult that pushes you to improve.
Done intentionally and with careful thought, especially to improve.

sentences.en: What does it really take to become an expert English speaker?
sentences.zh: 成为英语专家到底需要什么？

sentences.en: How do some people reach such a high level of fluency, while others seem to struggle for years without much progress?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人能达到极高的流利度，而另许多人似乎挣扎了多年却进展甚微？

sentences.en: Is it talent? Luck? Or something else? Recently, I rewatched a fascinating video from one of my favourite YouTube channels, Veritasium, titled “The Four Things It Takes to Be an Expert.” The video looks at the science behind how people become truly skilled at something, whether it’s music, sports, or academic subjects.
sentences.zh: 是天赋？运气？还是别的东西？最近，我重温了我最喜欢的 YouTube 频道之一 Veritasium 的一个精彩视频，标题是“成为专家所需的四件事”。该视频探讨了人们如何真正精通某项技能（无论是音乐、体育还是学术科目）背后的科学。

sentences.en: As I watched, I realised that the ideas in the video are incredibly relevant to English learners.
sentences.zh: 观看时，我意识到视频中的观点与英语学习者高度相关。

sentences.en: So, in this episode of Thinking in English, I want to take the four key principles from that Veritasium video and apply them directly to learning English.
sentences.zh: 因此，在本期 Thinking in English 节目中，我想提取 Veritasium 视频中的四个核心原则，并将其直接应用到英语学习中。

sentences.en: These principles can help guide your study, improve your skills, and ultimately help you become an expert speaker of the language.
sentences.zh: 这些原则可以帮助指导你的学习，提升你的技能，并最终帮助你成为该语言的专家级发言者。

sentences.en: This episode was originally recorded as a Bonus Episode for my Patreon community a year ago… subscribe to Patreon for more great episodes.
sentences.zh: 这集节目一年前最初是为我的 Patreon 社区录制的专属节目……订阅 Patreon 获取更多精彩节目。

sentences.en: Let’s get started!
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧！

sentences.en: Before we can talk about how to become an expert, we first need to ask: What actually is an expert?
sentences.zh: 在我们讨论如何成为专家之前，我们首先需要问：到底什么才是专家？

sentences.en: Collins Dictionary defines an expert as a person who is “very skilled at doing something or who knows a lot about a particular subject.” That’s a good starting point… but it doesn’t fully capture what makes someone truly expert.
sentences.zh: 柯林斯词典将专家定义为“非常擅长做某事或对某个特定主题了解很多的人”。这是一个很好的起点……但它并没有完全涵盖真正专家之所以为专家的核心。

sentences.en: In the Veritasium video, they argue that what separates experts from the rest of us isn’t just knowledge or years of study, it’s something more specific: recognition, which is deeply tied to long-term memory.
sentences.zh: 在 Veritasium 的视频中，他们认为将专家与我们其他人区分开来的不仅是知识或多年的学习，而是一个更具体的东西：认知，这与长期记忆深切相关。

sentences.en: Let me give you an example. There’s a popular YouTube channel called Drumeo, where they invite some of the world’s best drummers to perform in their studio.
sentences.zh: 我举个例子。有一个名为 Drumeo 的热门 YouTube 频道，他们邀请世界上一些最优秀的鼓手到他们的工作室表演。

sentences.en: One of their most impressive challenges is this: they play a famous song without the drum track, and ask the drummer to add their own version without ever hearing the original.
sentences.zh: 他们最令人印象深刻的挑战之一是：他们在没有鼓点音轨的情况下播放一首名曲，并要求鼓手在从未听过原版的情况下加入他们自己的版本。

sentences.en: Most of the pros take a little time, maybe a few listens, some quick notes, and then give it a go.
sentences.zh: 大多数专业鼓手需要花一点时间，听几次，做一些简单的笔记，然后尝试一下。

sentences.en: But then there’s Chad Smith, the drummer for the Red Hot Chili Peppers.
sentences.zh: 但红辣椒乐队（Red Hot Chili Peppers）的鼓手查德·史密斯（Chad Smith）却不修边幅。

sentences.en: Within 30 seconds of hearing a brand-new song, he can jump in and play a drum part that fits perfectly, and often sounds even better than the original.
sentences.zh: 在听到一首全新歌曲的 30 秒内，他就可以切入并演奏一段完美契合的鼓点，而且通常听起来比原版还要好。

sentences.en: He instinctively knows the rhythm, structure, tone, and energy of the track without needing to think.
sentences.zh: 他无需思考，就能本能地知道该曲目的节奏、结构、音调和能量。

sentences.en: That’s recognition in action. It comes from decades of deliberate practice.
sentences.zh: 这就是行动中的认知。它来自于几十年的刻意练习。

sentences.en: He’s not guessing. His brain is identifying patterns, rhythms, and structures instantly, because they’ve become deeply embedded in his long-term memory.
sentences.zh: 他不是在瞎猜。他的大脑正在即时识别模式、节奏和结构，因为这些已经深深植入他的长期记忆中。

sentences.en: This is the kind of recognition that defines expertise.
sentences.zh: 这种认知正是专业水平的定义。

sentences.en: And it’s the same in language learning. When you hear a sentence in English and immediately understand it, or when you respond automatically with the right word or grammar pattern, that’s recognition at work.
sentences.zh: 语言学习也是如此。当你听到一句英语并立即理解它，或者当你用正确的单词或语法模式自动回应时，这就是认知在发挥作用。

sentences.en: You don’t need to think through every rule.
sentences.zh: 你不需要把每个规则都想一遍。

sentences.en: You don’t need to translate. You just know it.
sentences.zh: 你不需要翻译。你自然而然就知道。

sentences.en: That’s a sign you’re moving toward expertise.
sentences.zh: 这是你正在向专业水平迈进的迹象。

sentences.en: The first key to becoming an expert is simple, but powerful: you need repeated attempts.
sentences.zh: 成为专家的第一个关键很简单，但很有力量：你需要重复尝试。

sentences.en: In other words, you need to practice. A lot.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你需要练习。大量的练习。

sentences.en: This probably isn’t surprising. We all know that to get better at something, you need to do it many times.
sentences.zh: 这可能并不令人意外。我们都知道，要想精通某事，你需要做很多次。

sentences.en: But it’s not just about repetition… it’s about intentional and consistent repetition with feedback.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是重复……而是带着反馈的有意识且持续的重复。

sentences.en: Think about a golfer.
sentences.zh: 想想高尔夫球手。

sentences.en: Before they ever become great, they’ve hit thousands and thousands of golf balls.
sentences.zh: 在他们变得伟大之前，他们已经击打了成千上万个高尔夫球。

sentences.en: They spend hours on the driving range, working on their swing, adjusting their stance, and improving their technique.
sentences.zh: 他们在练习场上花费数小时，打磨挥杆，调整姿势，提升技术。

sentences.en: Or take Phil Taylor, one of the greatest darts players of all time.
sentences.zh: 或者以菲尔·泰勒（Phil Taylor）为例，他是史上最伟大的飞镖选手之一。

sentences.en: His routine? Practicing darts six hours a day, every day, for over 20 years.
sentences.zh: 他的日常？每天练习飞镖六个小时，日复一日，持续了 20 多年。

sentences.en: Let’s do the maths: if he threw three darts per minute, which is probably a slow estimate, that’s nearly 8 million darts over two decades.
sentences.zh: 我们来算一算：如果他每分钟投三支飞镖，这可能还是个保守估计，那在二十年里就是将近 800 万支飞镖。

sentences.en: That’s the level of repetition it takes to become world-class at something.
sentences.zh: 这就是在一门技能上达到世界级水平所需的重复量。

sentences.en: But here’s the crucial part: when you practice skills like golf or darts, you get immediate feedback.
sentences.zh: 但最关键的部分来了：当你练习高尔夫或飞镖之类的技能时，你会得到即时反馈。

sentences.en: You know straight away whether your shot was good or bad.
sentences.zh: 你马上就知道你的击球是好是坏。

sentences.en: You adjust, try again, and improve. Now think about English learning.
sentences.zh: 你调整、再试一次、然后改进。现在想想英语学习。

sentences.en: If you want to become fluent, confident, and natural in English, you need the same mindset.
sentences.zh: 如果你想在英语中变得流利、自信和自然，你也需要这种心态。

sentences.en: You can’t expect to learn the second conditional or master pronunciation just by reading about it once in a textbook.
sentences.zh: 你不能指望仅仅通过在教科书里读一遍就学会第二条件句或掌握发音。

sentences.en: You need to use it, again and again and again.
sentences.zh: 你需要使用它，一次又一次，一遍又一遍。

sentences.en: In conversations. In writing. In exercises.
sentences.zh: 在对话中。在写作中。在练习中。

sentences.en: In real life. And just like with sports, you need to know whether your attempts are working.
sentences.zh: 在现实生活中。就像运动一样，你需要知道你的尝试是否有效。

sentences.en: You can practice speaking, writing, reading, and listening to English every day.
sentences.zh: 你可以每天练习说、写、读、听英语。

sentences.en: You can answer hundreds of grammar questions, take part in dozens of conversations, and get better with every single attempt, as long as you’re checking and learning from your results.
sentences.zh: 只要你检查并从结果中学习，你就可以回答数百个语法问题，参与数十次对话，并且每一次尝试都会让你变得更好。

sentences.en: This is one reason I always tell learners: don’t do a grammar worksheet and then forget to check your answers.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我总是告诉学习者：做完语法练习千万别忘了核对答案。

sentences.en: That feedback is essential. Otherwise, you might be repeating mistakes instead of improving.
sentences.zh: 这种反馈至关重要。否则，你可能是在重复错误，而不是在进步。

sentences.en: Feedback doesn’t have to come from a teacher, though that’s ideal.
sentences.zh: 反馈不一定非得来自老师，尽管那是理想情况。

sentences.en: You can get feedback from apps, answer keys, friends, or conversation partners.
sentences.zh: 你可以从应用程序、答案解析、朋友或对话伙伴那里获得反馈。

sentences.en: The more often you try, and the more clearly you know what works and what doesn’t, the faster you’ll improve.
sentences.zh: 你尝试得越频繁，而且越清楚什么有效、什么无效，你进步的速度就会越快。

sentences.en: So, you’re making repeated attempts and practicing regularly.
sentences.zh: 所以，你正在进行重复尝试并定期练习。

sentences.en: Great! But here’s an important question: Are you practicing in the right kind of environment?
sentences.zh: 很好！但这里有一个重要问题：你的练习环境对吗？

sentences.en: According to Veritasium, the second key to becoming an expert is working within a valid environment.
sentences.zh: 根据 Veritasium 的说法，成为专家的第二个关键是在一个有效的环境中工作。

sentences.en: What does that mean? A valid environment is one that has rules, patterns, and consistency.
sentences.zh: 这是什么意思？一个有效的环境是指具有规则、模式和一致性的环境。

sentences.en: It’s an environment where, with enough experience and feedback, you can actually improve.
sentences.zh: 在这个环境中，只要有足够的经验和反馈，你确实可以取得进步。

sentences.en: Let me give you an example. Imagine flipping a coin 10,000 times.
sentences.zh: 我举个例子。想象一下抛硬币 10,000 次。

sentences.en: Each time, you try to guess whether it’ll land heads or tails.
sentences.zh: 每一次，你都试图猜出它是正面朝上还是反面朝上。

sentences.en: You get immediate feedback every time, you know if you were right or wrong.
sentences.zh: 你每次都能得到即时反馈，你知道自己猜对还是猜错。

sentences.en: And you’ve got repeated attempts.
sentences.zh: 而且你有很多次重复尝试。

sentences.en: Sounds like a perfect learning environment, right?
sentences.zh: 听起来是个完美的学习环境，对吧？

sentences.en: Not really. Why? Because coin flips are random.
sentences.zh: 并不尽然。为什么？因为抛硬币是随机的。

sentences.en: There are no patterns to learn, no rules to master.
sentences.zh: 没有要学习的模式，也没有要掌握的规则。

sentences.en: It doesn’t matter how many times you try, you won’t become better at predicting it.
sentences.zh: 不管你尝试多少次，你预测它的能力都不会提高。

sentences.en: The environment isn’t valid for learning.
sentences.zh: 这个环境对学习来说是无效的。

sentences.en: English is not random. It has patterns, structure, grammar rules, vocabulary systems, and pronunciation logic.
sentences.zh: 英语不是随机的。它有模式、结构、语法规则、词汇系统和发音逻辑。

sentences.en: Of course, it’s complex, and sometimes it feels irregular, but it’s still a valid learning environment.
sentences.zh: 当然，它很复杂，有时感觉不规则，但它仍然是一个有效的学习环境。

sentences.en: You can improve over time because there are things to notice, remember, and predict.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，你可以进步，因为有东西可以去注意、去记住、去预测。

sentences.en: For example: In short: Languages are learnable.
sentences.zh: 例如：总而言之：语言是可学习的。

sentences.en: And that’s good news. But this also means that not all “study environments” are equally useful.
sentences.zh: 这是好消息。但这同时也意味着并非所有的“学习环境”都同样有用。

sentences.en: Random YouTube videos with no subtitles, or watching a movie without trying to understand anything, might not be the most valid environment for improvement.
sentences.zh: 没有字幕的随机 YouTube 视频，或者不求甚解地看电影，可能并不是最有效的提升环境。

sentences.en: But a conversation with a tutor, a challenging grammar exercise, a reading passage with vocabulary support, those are valid environments where learning actually happens.
sentences.zh: 但是与导师的对话、具有挑战性的语法练习、带有词汇支持的阅读文章，这些都是真正发生学习的有效环境。

sentences.en: So far, we’ve talked about the importance of repeated attempts and practicing in a valid environment.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，我们已经讨论了重复尝试和在有效环境中练习的重要性。

sentences.en: But how do you actually know if you’re improving?
sentences.zh: 但你如何真正知道自己是否在进步呢？

sentences.en: That brings us to the third key to becoming an expert: timely feedback.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了成为专家的第三个关键：及时的反馈。

sentences.en: Feedback is how you learn from your actions.
sentences.zh: 反馈是你从行动中学习的方式。

sentences.en: It helps you correct mistakes, adjust your strategy, and reinforce the right patterns.
sentences.zh: 它帮助你纠正错误、调整策略并巩固正确的模式。

sentences.en: But here’s the crucial point: the timing of the feedback really matters.
sentences.zh: 但关键点在这里：反馈的时机真的很重要。

sentences.en: There’s a big difference between immediate feedback and delayed feedback.
sentences.zh: 即时反馈和延迟反馈之间有很大的区别。

sentences.en: Let’s go back to the golf example. A golfer hits the ball and immediately sees where it goes.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到高尔夫的例子。高尔夫球手击球后立即看到球的去向。

sentences.en: They can tell right away if the shot was too short, too far, or off to the side.
sentences.zh: 他们马上就能看出这一击是太近、太远，还是偏向了一侧。

sentences.en: Then they adjust, try again, and improve… shot by shot.
sentences.zh: 然后他们调整、再试一次、然后改进……一次一球。

sentences.en: But now think about a university admissions officer.
sentences.zh: 但现在想想大学招生官。

sentences.en: They receive thousands of applications and have to decide who gets accepted.
sentences.zh: 他们收到数千份申请，必须决定谁能被录取。

sentences.en: Their goal is to choose students who will succeed academically.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是挑选出能在学业上取得成功的学生。

sentences.en: But here’s the problem: they don’t find out whether they made the right decision until months or even years later, when those students eventually take exams or graduate.
sentences.zh: 但问题来了：直到几个月甚至几年后，当这些学生最终参加考试或毕业时，他们才知道自己是否做出了正确的决定。

sentences.en: Because the feedback is so delayed, and so limited, it’s hard for them to learn or improve their selection process.
sentences.zh: 因为反馈如此滞后且有限，他们很难从中学习或改进他们的筛选流程。

sentences.en: In fact, studies show that university admissions teams and job recruiters are often poor at predicting long-term performance.
sentences.zh: 事实上，研究表明，大学招生团队和招聘人员往往很难预测长期的表现。

sentences.en: Why? Because feedback arrives too slowly to help them adjust.
sentences.zh: 为什么？因为反馈来得太慢，无法帮助他们调整。

sentences.en: Now let’s bring it back to English learning.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们把它拉回到英语学习中。

sentences.en: Imagine doing 50 grammar questions and then never checking your answers.
sentences.zh: 想象一下做了 50 个语法题，然后从来不核对答案。

sentences.en: Or checking them a week later when you’ve forgotten how you were thinking.
sentences.zh: 或者在一周后你已经忘了当时是怎么想的才去核对。

sentences.en: That kind of delayed feedback is nearly useless.
sentences.zh: 那种延迟的反馈几乎毫无用处。

sentences.en: To improve quickly and effectively you need fast, clear feedback that helps you understand what you did right or wrong while the memory is still fresh.
sentences.zh: 为了快速有效地提高，你需要快速、清晰的反馈，帮助你在记忆犹新时理解自己做对了什么或做错了什么。

sentences.en: So how can you get timely feedback when learning English?
sentences.zh: 那么在学习英语时，你如何获得及时的反馈呢？

sentences.en: The faster you know whether you’re right or wrong, the faster you can improve.
sentences.zh: 你越快知道自己是对是错，你就能越快进步。

sentences.en: So, you’re practicing regularly. You’re in a valid environment.
sentences.zh: 所以，你一直在定期练习。你身处一个有效的环境中。

sentences.en: You’re getting feedback quickly. Is that enough?
sentences.zh: 你正在迅速获得反馈。这就够了吗？

sentences.en: Not quite. There’s one more ingredient that separates average learners from expert learners.
sentences.zh: 还不够。还有一个因素将普通学习者与专家学习者区分开来。

sentences.en: You need to be constantly challenged. Veritasium puts it like this: “To learn, you need to be practicing at the edge of your ability.”
sentences.zh: 你需要不断接受挑战。Veritasium 是这样说的：“要学习，你需要在能力边缘进行练习。”

sentences.en: Let me explain why it matters. When you’re doing something that’s too easy, you’re not really growing.
sentences.zh: 让我解释一下为什么这很重要。当你做一些太容易的事情时，你并没有真正的成长。

sentences.en: You’re just repeating what you already know.
sentences.zh: 你只是在重复你已经知道的东西。

sentences.en: That can feel comfortable, but your brain isn’t building new connections or reinforcing deeper understanding.
sentences.zh: 这可能感觉很舒服，但你的大脑并没有建立新的连接或巩固更深层的理解。

sentences.en: When I first started learning Japanese back in 2016, I made incredibly fast progress.
sentences.zh: 2016 年我刚开始学日语时，我的进步速度快得惊人。

sentences.en: In just eight months, I passed an exam that usually takes most learners a few years to prepare for.
sentences.zh: 仅仅八个月，我就通过了一项通常需要大多数学习者准备好几年的考试。

sentences.en: Why? Because I was constantly pushing myself to do things that were just a little too difficult.
sentences.zh: 为什么？因为我不断逼自己去做那些对我来说稍微有点难的事情。

sentences.en: I studied textbooks far above my level. I struggled, failed, got confused, and then studied even harder to catch up.
sentences.zh: 我学习远超我水平的教科书。我挣扎、失败、感到困惑，然后更加努力地学习以赶上进度。

sentences.en: That effort made me improve faster than I thought was possible.
sentences.zh: 这种努力让我的进步速度超过了我认为的极限。

sentences.en: But then I left Japan and went back to the UK.
sentences.zh: 但后来我离开日本回到了英国。

sentences.en: I stopped challenging myself, and as a result, my Japanese ability plateaued.
sentences.zh: 我停止了挑战自我，结果我的日语能力进入了瓶颈期。

sentences.en: It stayed the same. I wasn’t getting worse… but I wasn’t getting better either.
sentences.zh: 它停滞不前了。我没有变差……但也没有变好。

sentences.en: And this happens in language learning all the time.
sentences.zh: 这种情况在语言学习中一直在发生。

sentences.en: You might listen to the same podcasts, read the same level of books, or use the same grammar exercises, and feel like you’re doing something useful.
sentences.zh: 你可能会听相同的播客，读相同水平的书籍，或者使用相同的语法练习，并且觉得你正在做一些有用的事情。

sentences.en: But if you’re not operating near the edge of your current ability, you’re not making serious progress.
sentences.zh: 但如果你没有在当前能力的边缘运作，你就没有取得实质性的进展。

sentences.en: Experts are different. They don’t stop when things get easy, they find new, harder challenges.
sentences.zh: 专家则不同。当事情变得容易时他们不会停下来，他们会寻找新的、更具挑战性的挑战。

sentences.en: They increase the weight, speed, or difficulty.
sentences.zh: 他们增加重量、速度或难度。

sentences.en: They push through frustration and confusion.
sentences.zh: 他们冲破挫折和困惑。

sentences.en: They stay just outside their comfort zone, all the time.
sentences.zh: 他们一直让自己处于舒适区边缘。

sentences.en: That’s called deliberate practice. Deliberate practice means doing something slightly beyond your current level and thinking carefully about how to improve.
sentences.zh: 这被称为刻意练习。刻意练习意味着做一些略超你当前水平的事情，并仔细思考如何改进。

sentences.en: It’s different from passive repetition. Here’s another example: learning to drive.
sentences.zh: 这与被动重复不同。这里有另一个例子：学开车。

sentences.en: At the beginning, driving is hard. You’re thinking about everything: mirrors, indicators, braking, steering, road signs.
sentences.zh: 一开始，开车很难。你要考虑所有事情：后视镜、转向灯、刹车、方向盘、道路标志。

sentences.en: It’s overwhelming. But after a while, it becomes automatic.
sentences.zh: 这让人不知所措。但过了一会儿，它就变成自动的了。

sentences.en: You no longer think about every action, you just drive.
sentences.zh: 你不再考虑每一个动作，你只是在开车。

sentences.en: At that point, most people stop improving.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，大多数人停止了进步。

sentences.en: You’ve reached a functional, comfortable level… and you stay there.
sentences.zh: 你达到了一个功能性的、舒适的水平……然后就停在那里了。

sentences.en: But a Formula 1 driver or rally racer? They don’t stop.
sentences.zh: 但 F1 车手或拉力赛车手呢？他们不会停下来。

sentences.en: They keep driving faster cars, in more difficult conditions, pushing their reaction time, precision, and performance every time they get behind the wheel.
sentences.zh: 他们继续驾驶更快的车，在更困难的条件下，每次坐到方向盘后面时都在挑战他们的反应时间、精确度和表现。

sentences.en: They stay at the edge of their ability. If you want to become an expert English speaker, you need to do the same.
sentences.zh: 他们停留在能力的边缘。如果你想成为一名英语专家，你也需要这样做。

sentences.en: In fact, this might not be the best business advice for me, but if Thinking in English ever feels too easy, you should consider moving on to more difficult materials.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这对我来说可能不是最好的商业建议，但如果 Thinking in English 让你觉得太容易了，你应该考虑转向更难的材料。

sentences.en: Native podcasts, books, or news articles might be the next step in your journey.
sentences.zh: 原版播客、书籍或新闻文章可能是你旅程中的下一步。

sentences.en: Of course, don’t jump into something too hard.
sentences.zh: 当然，不要直接跳到太难的东西上。

sentences.en: If you’re a beginner, don’t join an advanced discussion group.
sentences.zh: 如果你是初学者，不要加入高级讨论组。

sentences.en: But find something just slightly above your level, something that forces you to grow.
sentences.zh: 但要找到略高于你水平的东西，能迫使你成长的事物。

sentences.en: That’s the mindset of an expert: never staying comfortable.
sentences.zh: 这就是专家的心态：绝不满足于舒适。

sentences.en: Always improving.
sentences.zh: 永远在进步。

sentences.en: So, what does it really take to become an expert?
sentences.zh: 那么，成为专家到底需要什么？

sentences.en: It’s about how you practice, how you learn, and how you respond to challenges.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你是如何练习的，你是如何学习的，以及你如何应对挑战。

sentences.en: The four key ingredients to becoming an expert are:
sentences.zh: 成为专家的四个核心要素是：

sentences.en: If you can bring these four things together in your English study routine, you’ll start seeing meaningful development in how you use and understand the language.
sentences.zh: 如果你能将这四点融合到你的英语学习日常中，你就会开始看到你在使用和理解这门语言的方式上取得有意义的发展。

sentences.en: Maybe the most important message from this episode is this: Don’t be comfortable.
sentences.zh: 也许这一集最重要的信息是：不要贪图舒适。

sentences.en: Be challenged. What do you think? How are you going to become an expert at English?
sentences.zh: 去接受挑战。你觉得呢？你打算如何成为英语专家？
